newsitem.title: USA: Hartford leaders abandon effort to save Whalers.
newsitem.headline: Hartford leaders abandon effort to save Whalers.

text.p: A group of corporate leaders have reluctantly given up their last-ditch attempt to broker an agreement that would keep the Hartford Whalers in the capital city, the group's spokesman said on Thursday.
"The business leaders have decided that at this point, no further efforts are appropriate," said Thomas Groark, former chairman of the Greater Hartford Chamber of Commerce.
Groark told Reuters that Whalers officials seemed unwilling to participate in any talks.

Team owner Peter Karmanos last week rejected Connecticut Governor John Rowland's proposal to build a $147 million arena, and said the National Hockey League (NHL) team would leave the state at the end of the season.
Karmanos has not said where the team, which came to Hartford in 1975, will relocate. Among the cities seen as contenders are Minneapolis/St. Paul, Minn.; Columbus, Ohio; Nashville and Oklahoma City.

The Whalers were Connecticut's only major league sports franchise. They contributed about a third of the $200 million a year pumped into Hartford's economy by the arts, entertainment and sports, according to a recent study.
The corporate leaders were offering Karmanos $2 million more a year to sweeten the revenue a proposed sports arena in Hartford would earn for the Whalers.
The Whalers last week said there was a gap of $6 million a year in what the arena would earn the team and what it needed to compete with other NHL franchises.
The team was also displeased about the $45 million in operating losses it would have suffered in three seasons while a new arena was being built. -- Hartford newsroom (860) 727-0224
